solutions.title: Travel Time Estimation Against Nearby DCs

quiz.question: How do delivery systems efficiently aggregate inventory across multiple warehouse locations?
options: Use only the largest warehouse within delivery range
quiz.explanation: Effective availability is the union of inventory in every DC that can deliver within the time window, so quantities are summed.

quiz.question: Why is straight-line distance a poor way to decide which DCs can deliver within 1 hour?
options: It is too expensive to compute
Real travel time depends on roads and traffic, not distance
Latitude and longitude are not precise enough
quiz.explanation: Two DCs at the same distance can have very different drive times, so a travel-time estimate is needed.

quiz.question: What guarantees two customers can't both buy the last unit of an item?
options: A cache with a long TTL
A database transaction over the inventory rows
quiz.explanation: Ordering requires strong consistency: decrement inventory and create the order atomically in one transaction.

quiz.question: Why can the list of DCs be kept in the availability service's memory?
quiz.explanation: DCs are buildings — they change rarely — so syncing them periodically into memory is safe and fast.
